title: Polyglot stable interfaces for streaming/tool-calls/typed outputs
creator: Asha Raman
description:
Overview:
This ticket delivers a set of language idiomatic interfaces and examples (TypeScript, Python, Go) that establish a stable contract for three combined features: streaming generation, tool/function calling, and structured JSON/YAML outputs. The goal is a minimal, well-tested compatibility layer that existing clients can adopt with a single import/upgrade and that new clients can use natively.

Goals:
- Define a canonical, language-agnostic event envelope model for streaming responses that includes typed tool-invocation events and typed structured-output events.
- Provide small, ergonomic wrappers in TS/Py/Go that map runtime events to language types and callbacks/promises/iterators.
- Ensure backward compatibility with previous streaming shape (delta + done) while surfacing tool calls and structured outputs in a first-class way.
- Ship examples and migration guide that cover: simple stream-to-text, streaming tool invocation with arguments/response, progressive structured JSON (with partial parse and validation), error handling and fallback model routing.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Envelope model: chosen single-event-kind envelope with keys: kind, payload, token, offset, meta. This adds a small extra wrapper vs raw tokens but makes tool and structure events unambiguous across languages. Trade-off: slightly larger wire payload; benefit: deterministic parsing and easier error recovery.
- Type surface: provide strict TypeScript interfaces, lightweight dataclasses in Python (pydantic-lite), and simple structs in Go. We intentionally avoid heavy codegen in first iteration to accelerate adoption; follow-up ticket will add optional codegen from a canonical schema.
- Backwards compatibility: we will accept both legacy streaming tokens and the new envelope. The SDK will attempt envelope parse first and fall back to legacy token stream. This keeps current customers working while encouraging migration.

Acceptance criteria:
- Core interfaces published in monorepo packages for ts/py/go with exported types and runtime adapters.
- End-to-end examples in examples/ showing: (1) stream-only chat, (2) stream with tool call and tool response, (3) streaming structured JSON with progressive validation.
- Integration tests that run against the hosted staging runtime (staging-redwood) validating event ordering and tool-call roundtrips.
- Migration doc and quickstart guides landing in docs/sdks and referenced in Console docs.

Implementation notes:
- TS: add StreamingEnvelope type, StreamReader async iterable helper, toolCall callback signature (name: string, args: Record<string, any>), and structuredOutput parser (tries incremental JSON parse then emits validated objects). Example use: const iter = client.stream(...); for await (const evt of iter) { if (evt.kind === 'tool_call') await tools.invoke(evt.payload) }
- Python: StreamIterator yields StreamingEvent typed NamedTuple; provide async generator adapter that yields TokenDelta events and raises ToolInvocation exceptions with attached metadata to simplify sync clients.
- Go: Provide channel-based iterator and small stateful parser that emits enum-kind events and a helper to attach user callbacks for tool invocations. Keep API minimal to avoid blocking goroutine patterns.

Testing and rollout:
- Unit tests per-language that validate parsing of mixed envelope+legacy streams, produce reproducible ordering tests.
- E2E tests in staging that exercise tool-call flows with a sandbox tool (github-sandbox) and assert correct handoff and resume semantics.
- Canary rollout: default new clients to opt-in with header X-SDK-Streaming-Envelope: beta, then flip to default after 2 weeks of canary telemetry.

Telemetry and observability:
- Emit event metric sdk.streaming.envelope_parse_errors and sdk.streaming.tool_invocations with tags for language and client-version.
- Add trace spans for tool-invocation handoff to Redwood tool router.

Migration guide summary (to land in docs):
- How to detect if you are receiving legacy tokens or envelopes.
- Minimal code snippets to adapt: TS async-iter example, Python sync wrapper using sync_from_async, Go channel adapter.
- Known incompatibilities: older clients that inspect raw token stream for prompt-injection heuristics may need slight changes.

Links and artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFR/Streaming+Envelope+Design
- Working PR (TS): https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk/pull/2246
- Working PR (Py): https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk/pull/2249
- Working PR (Go): https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk/pull/2251
- Examples folder (draft): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB-Examples-SDK-Streaming
- Staging test run dashboard: https://monitoring.redwood.ai/dashboards/streams-canary

Next steps and open questions:
- Decide whether schema should be published as OpenAPI/JSON Schema for codegen (follow-up ticket suggested).
- Confirm KMS-sensitive tool-call metadata classification for security review.
- Finalize canary gating thresholds (error rate < 0.5%, parse errors < 0.1%).
